component.name: ai-prompt
component.title: AI Prompt
component.description: Expose a Camel route as a prompt that MCP clients list and get through the Camel MCP server.
component.label: ai

arguments.label: consumer
arguments.description: The arguments of the prompt, set as argument.NAME.description=TEXT and argument.NAME.required=true or false, where either option declares the argument NAME and an argument is optional by default. The route receives each argument as a String header named NAME; undeclared arguments of a request are ignored, and a request without a required argument is rejected before the route runs. A NAME that starts with camel or org.apache.camel. in any case is not allowed. This is a multi-value option with prefix: argument.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

configuration.description: The configuration that every endpoint starts from. The endpoint copies it, and the options of the endpoint URI replace its values.

description.label: consumer
description.description: The description of what the prompt provides, which MCP clients see in prompts/list and receive in the prompts/get result. If not set or blank, the prompt name is used.

tags.label: consumer
tags.description: A comma-separated list of tags to register the prompt under. The MCP server exposes the prompts whose tags match its tag patterns. Without tags, the prompt goes into a default pool that the MCP server never exposes.

title.label: consumer
title.description: The human-readable title of the prompt, which MCP clients can show in prompts/list instead of the name. If not set, the prompt has no title.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

consumerOut.description: No body is sent to the route. Each prompt argument is available as a message header with its configured argument name; values are strings.

consumerReply.description: A String, byte array, stream or file is converted to one user message. A List may contain Strings or Maps with role (user or assistant) and content. Content may be a String or an MCP content block.

promptName.description: The name of the prompt, which MCP clients see in prompts/list and pass to prompts/get. It must not contain a slash. A route whose prompt name is already registered under one of its tags, or in the pool of prompts without tags, fails to start.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
